THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLE 226 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA READ WITH SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C., PRAYING TO-i) QUASH THE FIR IN ANNEXURE A CRIME NO. 488/2023 REGISTERED FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTION 498A R/W 34 OF THE INDIAN PENAL CODE AND FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTION 3 AND 4 OF THE DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT AT ANNEXURE-A.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioners - husband and his family members are before this Court calling in question registration of a crime in Crime No.488/2023, pending before the V Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, for the offences under NC: 2024:KHC:37414 Sections 498A and 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2, in unison submit that the parties to the lis were before the family Court in M.C.No.2042/2023 and during the pendency the proceedings before the family Court, the parties have settled the dispute amicably among themselves by drawing up certain terms and conditions.
Respondent No.2 on her own will has agreed to withdraw the impugned proceedings.

A copy of the memorandum of settlement under Section 89 of CPC r/w.
Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005, is also appended to the petition.
An application under Section 359 r/w. 528 of the BNSS along with a joint affidavit is filed before this Court to that effect.

3. The memorandum of settlement filed by the parties reads as follows:
"MEMORANDUM OF SETTLEMENT UNDER SECTION 89 OF CPC READ WITH RULES 24 AND 25 OF THE KARNATAKA CIVIL PROCEDURE (MEDIATION)
RULES, 2005.
The Petitioner has filed this petition against the Respondent under Section 13 (1) (1-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 for dissolution of his marriage with the respondent.

sentences.text: The aforesaid petition was referred to mediation for resolving the dispute between the parties.

During the course of mediation, the parties along with their respective counsels have participated in the mediation process and the parties have resolved their dispute and have agreed to the following terms and conditions:
1. The petitioner and the respondent are Hindus by religion.

Their marriage was solemnized on 07.11.2021 at Jayanth Convention Center, No.9, Railway Layout, 2nd Stage, Ullal Main road, RTO Road, Vishweshwaraiah Layout, Bengaluru 560 058 as per Hindu rites and customs.
2. The parties state and admit that due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility of temperaments, they are living separately from March 2023.
The efforts made by the elders, friends and well wishers to resolve the differences between the parties did not yield any fruits.
There is absolutely no chance of a reunion between them.
The petitioner and the respondent know that their marriage is Irretrievably broken down and there are no chances of reunion to lead a happy married life.
Hence, the petitioner and the respondent have decided to get the marriage dissolved by a decree of divorce.
3. Both the parties state that they have no children born to them from their wedlock.
4. The petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Seventy Two Lakhs Only) to the respondent.

towards maintenance/permanent alimony in full and final settlement of all her claims by way of demand draft bearing No. 799594 dated 27.08.2024 drawn on Canara Bank, Girinagara Branch, Bengaluru and the same shall be handed over to the respondent at the time of reporting settlement before the NC:
2024:KHC:37414 Hon'ble Court.
The respondent has agreed for the same.

5. Further the petitioner is returning a sum of Rs.22,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lakhs Only) which was borrowed from his mother-in-law (respondent's mother) by way of demand draft bearing No.799593 dated 27.08.2024 drawn on Canara Bank,
Girinagara Branch, Bengaluru in favour of respondent's mother Smt. Mamatha M.N.
and the same shall be handed over to the respondent at the time of reporting settlement before the Hon'ble Court.
6.

The respondent/wife has agreed to return the cheque bearing No.811045 dated 30.04.2024 drawn on Axis Bank, Bengaluru (KT), Bengaluru which was given by the petitioner/husband to the respondent/wife for the settlement purpose and the same shall be handed over to the petitioner/husband at the time of reporting settlement before the Hon'ble Court.
The petitioner has agreed for the same.
7. Both parties state that they have already exchanged their valuable articles and personal belongings as such they have no claims in this regard.

9. The parties admit and agree that they have no further claims of whatsoever manner against each other either past, present or future.

10. In view of the settlement arrived between the parties they have agreed to withdraw/quash/close the following cases:
a) The respondent herein has agreed to co-operate with the petitioner here in closing/quashing Crime No. 488/2023 which is pending before 5th ACMM,
Bengaluru.
NC: 2024:KHC:37414 b) W.P.No.13741/2024 filed by the petitioner herein which is pending before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka for quashing of Crime No.488/2023.

c) C.C.25812/2024 which is filed by the respondent/wife against the petitioner/husband which is pending on the file of the 6th ACMM, Bengaluru.
d) Crime No.59/2024 filed by the petitioner herein which is pending before 6th ACMM, Bengaluru.

11. The petitioner undertakes to convince his mother to withdraw O.S.1412/2023 which is filed by her against the respondent and others which is pending before I Addl. Junior Division, Bengaluru Rural District Court, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: 12. The parties admit and agree that there is no coercion or force, fraud or any undue influence in filing the above petition and entering into this compromise in the aforesaid manner.
13. Both the parties admit that they shall not interfere in the lives of each other in future.

14. Both the parties agree that they will withdraw all the allegations made against each other either orally or expressly."
In the light of the fact that the parties have already parted their ways and arrived at settlement and as it is a marital dispute, I deem it appropriate to accept the application, joint affidavit and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are not against the State.

4. The petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Seventy Two Lakhs Only) to the respondent.
towards maintenance/permanent alimony in full and final settlement of all her claims by way of demand draft bearing No. 799594 dated 27.08.2024 drawn on Canara Bank, Girinagara Branch, Bengaluru and the same shall be handed over to the respondent at the time of reporting settlement before the NC:

The respondent has agreed for the same.
5. Further the petitioner is returning a sum of Rs.22,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lakhs Only) which was borrowed from his mother-in-law (respondent's mother) by way of demand draft bearing No.799593 dated 27.08.2024 drawn on Canara Bank,
Girinagara Branch, Bengaluru in favour of respondent's mother Smt. Mamatha M.N.
and the same shall be handed over to the respondent at the time of reporting settlement before the Hon'ble Court.
6.

8. The parties herein state and agree that they have no claims over movable or Immovable properties belonging to each other either existing or to be acquired or Inherited at a later stage.
9. The parties admit and agree that they have no further claims of whatsoever manner against each other either past, present or future.
10. In view of the settlement arrived between the parties they have agreed to withdraw/quash/close the following cases:
a) The respondent herein has agreed to co-operate with the petitioner here in closing/quashing Crime No. 488/2023 which is pending before 5th ACMM,
Bengaluru.
NC: 2024:KHC:37414 b) W.P.No.13741/2024 filed by the petitioner herein which is pending before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka for quashing of Crime No.488/2023.
11. The petitioner undertakes to convince his mother to withdraw O.S.1412/2023 which is filed by her against the respondent and others which is pending before I Addl. Junior Division, Bengaluru Rural District Court, Bengaluru.
12. The parties admit and agree that there is no coercion or force, fraud or any undue influence in filing the above petition and entering into this compromise in the aforesaid manner.
13. Both the parties admit that they shall not interfere in the lives of each other in future.
14. Both the parties agree that they will withdraw all the allegations made against each other either orally or expressly."
In the light of the fact that the parties have already parted their ways and arrived at settlement and as it is a marital dispute, I deem it appropriate to accept the application, joint affidavit and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are not against the State.

(i) The writ petition is disposed.
(ii) The impugned Crime No.488/2023, pending before the V Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, stands quashed.
